issue_context.title: performance.timerify doesn't return wrapped function's return value
comments: Seems like a bug to me indeed. The function is called as a constructor and it returns an instance of it instead of the true return value.

Caught by this bug today!

Workaround: using arrow function.
Note, node 14 do not have this bug. So it's the bug of rewriting it from C++ to JS :-)

review_comments: Thank you for your example. I  will fix it immediately.
I ran that code before I posted it - I'm not sure what you mean by "can't" but here is a link to show that it can https://jsfiddle.net/atuL1wjk/

> I ran that code before I posted it - I'm not sure what you mean by "can't" but here is a link to show that it can https://jsfiddle.net/atuL1wjk/

It's an Eslint error called `error  Unexpected return statement in constructor`. Should we alter the configs of Eslint?

```suggestion
    const result = new.target !== undefined ?
      ReflectConstruct(fn, args, fn) :
      ReflectApply(fn, this, args);
```
You marked this conversation as resolved but didn't take my suggestion. Is it because you disagree with it, or because you forgot to push?
@aduh95 wouldn't `new.target` not be `undefined` only if `timerified()` is called with `new` instead of `fn()`?
Yes, but that's the point. We want the `timerified` function to behave the same as the original function in both cases.
Ah, we are returning `timerified` from `timerify`. Yea, this makes sense :+1:
